pr.title: Item categories and a category filter on the list

acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks rows, UNIQUE, CHECK, nullable column, index and tagging.
test 'AC-2' checks the title-only insert and the FOREIGN KEY rejection.
test 'AC-3' checks id order and both li markups.
test 'AC-4' checks link order, hrefs, aria-current and an empty category.
Two 'AC-5' tests cover filtering, id order, current link and ignored extra parameters.
test 'AC-6' checks the message, no li and the links.
test 'AC-7' checks escaping, the encoded link, and that requesting the link lists the item.
it.each 'AC-8' covers all five inputs: 404, message, Go back link, script, no li and no nav.
Verified by review with a concrete browser step. The code in src/index.js follows it, but it adds a history.length > 1 guard the spec does not state (see finding).
routes.json has the route. tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers accept, whitespace and #. test/traffic.test.js covers the fake app recording the query. test/index.test.js 'AC-11' checks 2xx.
The existing tests are kept, with the First item assertion updated. The healthz, 404 and 405 handlers are unchanged.
test/apply-migrations.js drops in one batch with deferred FKs. The 'AC-13' test would fail if the reset left rows behind.

findings.what: The Go back script goes back only if the referrer is same-origin AND history.length > 1. The spec decision states only the same-origin referrer condition and explicitly rejects history.length > 1. The extra guard is a departure, and the PR body doesn't mention it.
findings.fix: Remove `&& history.length > 1`, so it reads `if (ours) { e.preventDefault(); history.back(); }`.

findings.what: State table coverage is partial. Row '/, no items' says filter links are shown with All current, but the empty-table test checks only 'No items yet.'. The 'Go back hidden' cell for the 200 rows is never asserted: no test checks that a 200 page has no 'Go back' or corrupted message.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert the links and All current. Add assertions to the 200-row tests that 'Go back' and 'corrupted' are absent.

findings.what: The script assertion is a loose regex on document.referrer, location.origin and history.back(). It would still pass with the extra history.length guard, so it doesn't pin the decided condition.
findings.fix: Assert the exact condition once the extra guard is removed.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent apart from the Go back guard.
All 13 items are met, but the Go back condition departs from the decision.
The tests would fail if the code were wrong. The state table has a gap. I did not run the suite here; CI runs it.
The SQL is parameterised, matching is exact, and the migration is additive.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded, queries are bound, and no instructions were planted in the repo.
The page is minimal HTML. aria-current is used and the Go back link works without JavaScript.
The Go back flow is not browser-tested. AC-10 is by review, and the spec puts a browser test out of scope.
The PR says the script goes back 'only when the referrer is same-origin' and leaves out the extra history.length condition. The other claims are true.
